text:
elaine: heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-selector change, noticed ~12% tokens/sec drop on 8k-seq workloads. anyone else?

rahul: saw it on canary too. $/M tokens up ~15% on p3 runs. quick spike on nightly perf.

marcus: linked perf dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/runs/1988 - shows baseline vs post-change.

elaine: profiling looks like a lot of tiny KV misses that cause fallback from flashv3 -> paged-attn when seq > ~4k. suspect hysteresis threshold too aggressive.

tara: confirmed: KV cache eviction spike at ~75% mem pressure, KV hit-rate drops and selector flips. cc @jin for traces.

jin: dumped a quick nvprof snippet, see below. main cost shift is tiny memcpy + paged kernel overhead.

```
# nvprof snippet (trimmed)
Time(%)  Time(ms)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Name
 45.2    1123.4     1    1123.4   flash_attention_forward
 26.8     665.0     4    166.3   paged_attention_forward
 10.1     250.3    10     25.0   device_to_device_memcpy
  8.3     205.6     6     34.3   kv_cache_miss_handler
```

marcus: experiment: increasing hysteresis window 0.15 -> 0.25 keeps kernel sticky to flashv3, tokens/sec returns to baseline, but short-seq tail latency up ~5ms. tradeoff.

elaine: i'd rather a KV-hit-aware policy: if KV_hit_rate > 0.9 prefer flashv3 even if recent misses triggered fallback. batch-aware rules too: if batch_size >= 8 and avg_seq > 1k favor flash.

rahul: also saw batching issue: continuous batching cancels when kernel switch occurs, which fragments batches and raises per-token cost. selector flips are expensive.

tara: repro steps I'm using: `./bench.sh --model llama2-70b --seq 8192 --batch 16 --kernel-selector=auto`

```
# sample bench output
variant    tokens/sec    p99 latency(ms)    $/M tokens
flashv3     42,800         210                8.9
paged       37,200         198               10.5
hybrid      39,600         205                9.4
```

jin: quick A/B with KV-hit-aware hysteresis: when KV_hit_rate > 0.9 persist flash for 30s -> tokens/sec +10%, $/M -9%. Will push patch.

elaine: perfect. also want a perf CI alert on $/M tokens regression per-target. can we add a metric to the perf pipeline?

perf-bot: perf-alert: build 2026-03-16 - tokens/sec drop >10% on 8k-seq tests for nightly. investigation needed.

rahul: i'll open a PR to kernel-selector with flag `kv_hysteresis` + unit tests + canary rollout plan.

tara: schedule canary tonight and watch perf dashboard + error budget. :thumbsup:

marcus: added a ci test to record $/M tokens per kernel variant to catch regressions earlier.

elaine: ok, thanks all. jin please paste PR link when ready and we can merge behind a feature flag for canary.
